data.narrative:
Helical Fusion, a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Takaya Taguchi and Junichi Miyazawa, has raised $98M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy firms: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

The stage-progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($98M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B progression yields an implied valuation of $186M. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while 5 same-sector nuclear peers exist, the narrow filter for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables returned fewer than three datapoints, making median benchmarking unreliable and risking circularity if forced across the broader sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $158M (low) to $214M (high), centered on $186M. This range reflects the mechanical application of stage-based progression from the capital-raised baseline. Primary uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.9x multiplier for this specific subsector, the absence of transaction comparables, and the early-stage nature of most private peers, which limits their direct comparability. Further data on Helical Fusion's technical milestones, burn rate, and partner commitments would refine the estimate.
